message.content: In domestic cats and many other felids, the **presence of a mane (or “mane‑like” hair growth) in males** is typically considered a dominant trait. In lions, the same principle applies: the allele that codes for the development of a mane is dominant over the allele that results in a lack of mane. Thus, if a lion inherits one copy of the mane allele from either parent, it will develop a mane. This is why most male lions have a mane while females do not—female lions inherit two copies of the recessive allele (since they are XX).
